candidate_relations.reason: An isolated beta2-glycoprotein IgA result does not establish antiphospholipid syndrome and does not explain the full febrile multisystem syndrome.
The normal platelet count and absence of reported consumptive coagulopathy do not support disseminated intravascular coagulation.
No streptococcal infection is established, and the record favors a nonbacterial multisystem inflammatory syndrome.
The record lacks epidermal detachment or mucosal involvement characteristic of Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
Acute kidney injury is a major organ manifestation in this case but not the multisystem final diagnosis.
Dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction is a cardiac manifestation rather than the full inflammatory syndrome.
The patient has shock clinically, but bacterial septic shock is a differential and does not capture the final multisystem inflammatory diagnosis.
There is no widespread epidermal detachment or mucosal necrosis to support toxic epidermal necrolysis.
